title: Princess Diana feared Prince Harry would ‘wither’ in Prince William’s shadow: expert
summary: Princess Diana worried Prince Harry would "wither" in Prince William's shadow, says royal expert, as secret 1991 recordings surface in new documentary.
story: Royal broadcaster Helena Chard says Prince Harry's reported Diana documentary won't be viewed as a peace offering, warning it could reignite tensions with his older brother, Prince William.

Princess Diana feared Prince Harry would struggle to find his place in the royal family while growing up in the shadow of his older brother and future king Prince William, according to a royal expert.

The late Princess of Wales’ concerns about her sons are back in the spotlight amid news of the upcoming three-part documentary "Diana Unheard," which will feature never-before-heard audio from roughly five hours of secret recordings that Diana made with her friend Dr. James Colthurst in 1991.

The documentary's producers told Deadline that the recordings, which were used in Andrew Morton’s explosive 1992 biography, "Diana: Her True Story," include the princess speaking candidly about her sons, William and the line of succession, as well as her troubled marriage to then-Prince Charles and other aspects of royal life.
PRINCE HARRY'S RUMORED DIANA FILM 'MIGHT FEEL LIKE ANOTHER BETRAYAL' TO PRINCE WILLIAM AS RIFT GROWS: EXPERT

While speaking with Fox News Digital, British royals expert Christopher Andersen shared his view that the recordings could reveal Diana's long-held concerns about the vastly different paths awaiting her sons.
"Diana worried from the beginning that Harry might wither in the shadow of his brother the future king," the "Kate!" author said.
Princess Diana feared that Prince Harry would struggle in the shadow of Prince William, according to a royal expert. (Georges De Keerle / FSP / Liaison Agency; Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
PRINCE WILLIAM'S ABSENCE SPEAKS VOLUMES AS KING CHARLES REUNITES WITH PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE: EXPERTS

"Even at a young age, William shared his mother's concerns and for the most part took great pains to spare his brother's feelings," Andersen continued. "It's very telling that, in his last conversation with Diana just hours before her death, William expressed his fear that a photo opportunity at Eton might leave Harry feeling ignored."

Diana died at age 36 in August 1997 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash.
KING CHARLES, PRINCE WILLIAM 'FURIOUS' AS PRINCESS DIANA'S BROTHER UNLEASHES EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS: EXPERTS

Hours before her death, Diana called William, then 15, from her hotel in Paris, according to Morton's biography. During what would become their final conversation, William reportedly told his mother that he had been asked to participate in a solo photocall to mark the beginning of his third year at Eton College and shared that he was deeply concerned the high-profile solo moment would make Harry, then 12, feel overshadowed and excluded.
Andersen said that Diana had concerns that Harry would be left with "deep-seated feelings of insecurity and gnawing self-doubt." (Photo by Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

According to Andersen, Diana had confidence that William, now 44, would succeed in his role as future king, but she was apprehensive over how the monarchy's heir-and-spare dynamic would affect Harry, now 42.
PRINCE GEORGE FOLLOWS PRINCE WILLIAM'S FOOTSTEPS AT ETON IN A CHANGING ROYAL WORLD: EXPERTS
"Kate!: The Courage, Grace, and Power of the Woman Who Will Be Queen" by Christopher Andersen is available now. (Gallery Books)

"Wise, sensitive, an old soul — these were some of the words that Diana used to describe William," Andersen said. "She saw him as being mature far beyond his years. While Diana knew much would be demanded of William in the future, she never doubted that he would be up to the task."

"Harry was another matter entirely," Andersen said. "The world saw Harry as a charming scamp, and there definitely was that side to him, but Diana knew better than anyone that always being in his brother's formidable shadow could leave the Spare with deep-seated feelings of insecurity and gnawing self-doubt."
PRINCE WILLIAM'S DOOR IS 'BOLTED SHUT' AS PRINCE HARRY PLANS UK RETURN WITH MEGHAN MARKLE, CHILDREN: EXPERT
However, Andersen expressed his opinion that Diana had faith in the strength of the bond between William and Harry and would not have foreseen their future estrangement.
"Looking back, it's so odd to remember how close the brothers truly were," he said. "They had their moments, as all siblings do, but the boys were always so emotionally dependent on each other."
Royal experts said that Diana believed the brothers shared an "unbreakable bond." (Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)
PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'PLAYING IT COOL' AS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURN TO THE UK: EXPERT

"Diana always felt that, whatever challenges they faced, William and Harry would weather the storm together," Andersen continued. "She viewed the brothers as a unit. As far as Diana was concerned, theirs was an unbreakable bond."

Royal expert Kinsey Schofield agreed that Diana did not fear that there would be a rift between the brothers but argued that the late princess worried more over William's burden as the future king than Harry's supporting role.
PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FACE 'SUSSEX CIRCUS' AS PRINCE GEORGE PREPARES FOR ETON: EXPERT

"Based on my research, Diana was more concerned about the pressures of royal life affecting her sons individually than the possibility of them becoming estranged," the host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" told Fox News Digital.

"Diana understood that William and Harry were destined for very different lives," Schofield continued. "William was born to be king. Harry was born to support him. She wanted them to remain close because she understood the importance of William having someone he could trust."
PRINCE HARRY’S PUSH TO GIVE ARCHIE, LILIBET ROYAL UPBRINGING EXPOSES ‘CONTRADICTION’ AFTER PALACE EXIT: EXPERT

"Prince William’s future weighed heavily on Diana because she understood the responsibility he would inherit," she added. "She knew that William would never have the freedom to simply walk away from his destiny. She spoke to him about the importance of finding a suitable and supportive partner. She believed in his leadership but worried about his reluctance as a child."

"Harry, on the other hand, had opportunities William would never enjoy. He could pursue his own interests, build a career around charitable causes, and enjoy a degree of independence that his brother couldn’t."
Schofield argued that Diana worried more that William would struggle with the burden of being future king. (Anwar Hussein/WireImage)
Schofield pointed out that Harry was once a favorite of the British public and celebrated for his achievements.
"He was enormously popular," Schofield said. "He had a successful military career, founded the Invictus Games, and was one of the most beloved members of the royal family."
"Harry wasn’t destined for failure because he was born second," she continued. "He had every opportunity to build a meaningful life within the institution."
"I think Diana would have been more concerned about William carrying the weight of the Crown than Harry having to share the spotlight," Schofield added.
The royal experts agreed that Diana would have been shocked and distraught over William and Harry's current estrangement.
"Diana would have been heartbroken, and it's hard for me to imagine that the split ever would have happened if she had been alive," Andersen said. "Things just wouldn't have gotten so out of hand."

"I think Diana would be devastated," Schofield told Fox News Digital. "Prince William and Harry shared an experience that very few people on earth could understand. They lost their mother in front of the entire world. That shared grief should have been something that united them for life."
Schofield said that the brothers should have been united by their shared grief over Diana's death. (Jeff Overs/BBC News & Current Affairs via Getty Images)

Reports of tensions between the brothers first emerged in 2018, with Harry publicly acknowledging the strain in their relationship the following year when he said the brothers were on "different paths."

The divide widened further after Harry and his wife Meghan Markle announced their decision to step down from their roles as working royals in January 2020. The two's relationship continued to deteriorate in subsequent years following Harry and Markle's bombshell 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, the couple's 2022 Netflix series "Harry & Meghan" and Harry's explosive 2023 memoir "Spare."
However, British royals expert Hilary Fordwich cautioned against viewing Diana's decades-old concerns through the lens of events that unfolded long after her death.

"Hearing tapes today made back in 1991 though shouldn’t be taken as a current verdict regarding events and complicated results of events Princess Diana isn’t tragically alive to witness," Fordwich told Fox News Digital.

While Diana herself was known for challenging royal conventions and became increasingly more independent following her 1992 separation from Charles, she continued carrying out public duties and remained committed to many of the causes she had championed as a working royal.
Andersen and Schofield said that Diana would not have supported Harry's decision to step away from royal duties. (Reuters)
Andersen and Schofield argued that Diana's rebellious streak does not necessarily mean she would have supported Harry's decision to leave royal duties and his subsequent actions.

"Diana definitely knew that Harry would have to forge his own path to some extent — certainly more so than William, whose role in royal life is preordained," Andersen said. "But I don't believe Diana would have approved of Harry abruptly bailing on the monarchy the way he did."

"True, Diana was a rule-breaker and a rebel, but she also had a strong sense of duty and of history," he continued. "Diana believed that Harry had an important role to play. Harry probably would never be king, but he was the son of one and, as such, had his own unique destiny to fulfill within the monarchy."

"Of course, Diana would have wanted, above all else, for her sons to be happy, but it never would have occurred to her that Harry would simply turn his back on the rest of the royal family," Andersen added.
"Diana might have sympathized with Harry’s frustrations, but I don’t believe that means she would have supported everything he’s done since leaving," Schofield said.
"Diana understood what it meant to feel trapped," she continued. "But Harry had choices his mother never enjoyed. And he exercised them."
Schofield said that Diana most wanted her sons to be "happy" and "close." (Rota/Pool/Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Whatever new insights the recordings may offer into Diana's private concerns, Schofield said they could serve as a reminder of the priorities that shaped her life as a mother.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"Diana wanted both her sons to be happy," Schofield said. "She wanted them to be close. And she wanted them to grow into compassionate men who understood their responsibilities to others."

"If these recordings remind Americans of anything, I hope it’s that Diana’s legacy belongs to both her sons," she said.

title: Amanda Seyfried faces harsh criticism as viewers rip her behavior in Elizabeth Holmes documentary
summary: Amanda Seyfried faces backlash after appearing in "You Can See Everything" documentary, where her shifting sympathy for Elizabeth Holmes sparked debate.
story: The Theranos fraudster is now sharing the the prison with newly transferred inmate, Ghislaine Maxwell. (Derek Shook for Fox News Digital)
Amanda Seyfried landed in the hot seat after her appearance in the latest Elizabeth Holmes documentary unleashed a wave of criticism online.

Seyfried surprised viewers when she appeared alongside Nathan Fielder in "You Can See Everything," a documentary that followed Holmes in the last 34 days leading up to the start of her prison sentence. Holmes reported to Federal Prison Camp Bryan on May 30, 2023.

Seyfried revisited her connection to the disgraced Theranos founder, whom she portrayed in Hulu's "The Dropout." The new documentary, released Oct. 16, explored Seyfried's evolving perspective on Holmes, including her reactions to Holmes' personal life and relationship with Billy Evans. Stepping back into Holmes' shoes for the documentary, Seyfried helped Fielder recreate conversations he had with the disgraced Theranos founder after she reported to prison.
Throughout the film, Seyfried grappled with her growing sympathy for Holmes, even as the convicted fraudster challenged the way the actress portrayed her in the Hulu series.

Other viewers piled on, accusing Seyfried of changing her tune when the scrutiny shifted toward her own role in bringing the Theranos scandal to television.

"Lots of 'women protecting women' posturing from her until she gets accused of perhaps also causing Elizabeth some degree of pain, after which she immediately deflects and starts engaging in female emotional manipulation by accusing Nathan of covering up for Elizabeth based on her 'intuition,'" another user said.

Not everyone agreed with the harsh criticism. Some viewers came to Seyfried's defense, arguing that her changing opinion of Holmes wasn't a sign of hypocrisy but rather an essential part of the documentary's larger message.

"imagine walking away from this blaming amanda seyfried," a user wrote. "the point is, amanda herself changes her opinion on elizabeth holmes. so does nathan fielder. so does the audience. thats the literal point."

title: Matthew McConaughey divides fans over independent voting plea ahead of midterms
summary: Matthew McConaughey's video urging Americans to rethink the two-party system drew fierce social media backlash ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
story: Actor and author Matthew McConaughey joins 'Fox & Friends' to discuss his journey of faith and how it inspired his new poetry book, 'Poems & Prayers.'

Matthew McConaughey's call to rethink America's two-party political system has sparked a heated debate on social media, with some critics accusing the Oscar-winning actor of promoting a "privileged perspective" ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

On Sunday, McConaughey took to social media and challenged the long-held notion that voting for an independent candidate is a wasted vote, arguing that just a handful of independent lawmakers could dramatically shift the balance of power in Washington.

"They've been telling us for years that an independent vote is a wasted vote," McConaughey said in a video shared on Instagram. "Well, a great question for our times is, has that unwasted vote been working out for you?"
MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY HINTS AT POLITICAL AMBITIONS AFTER MEETING WITH POPE LEO XIV IN VATICAN CITY

While the actor insisted he was not endorsing a particular candidate or political party, his message quickly drew criticism from social media users who questioned the timing of his remarks and warned against encouraging independent voting ahead of November's elections.
"This message is so irresponsible right now. Do the math. Willie Nelson would not be impressed," one user commented.
Another accused the Hollywood star of being out of touch with the challenges facing everyday Americans.

"I understand that you're in a tax bracket where government decisions don't affect you like it does majority of constituents, but this isn't the time my guy," the user wrote. "Our government is doing their damnest to silence the lower and middle classes. These are incredibly dangerous times and we've got to get this administration OUT."
McConaughey argued that independent voters deserve a greater voice in Washington. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
A third critic slammed McConaughey's message as "ridiculous," arguing that his celebrity status and financial security bar him from facing the consequences of political decisions.
"This is a ridiculous, privileged perspective from someone with nothing to lose either way," the commenter wrote.

"Both sides absolutely have faults but one is dragging us deeper into cruel chaos, a broken economy, abducting our neighbors off the street, enforcing violence on its own citizens, stripping women of rights, trying actively to take away this vote you're encouraging people to utilize," the user continued.
"If you're gonna hop on instagram with your quick hot take this close to a crucial election period, at least say something substantive and try to stand on the correct side."
Despite the backlash, others rushed to McConaughey's defense, praising the actor for challenging political divisions and encouraging Americans to consider alternatives to the two major parties.

title: Prince Harry risks 'lobbing a grenade' at Prince William as chance to heal yearslong feud emerges: expert
summary: Prince Harry's reported Princess Diana documentary plans could derail reconciliation with Prince William, royal experts warn of deepening rift.
story: Royal broadcaster Helena Chard says Prince Harry's reported Diana documentary won't be viewed as a peace offering, warning it could reignite tensions with his older brother, Prince William.
Prince Harry’s return to the U.K. could offer him his best chance yet to reconcile with his estranged brother, Prince William, but royal experts say a major obstacle remains in his way.
A source told People magazine that Harry's return to Britain presents the "best opportunity" to repair his fractured relationship with Prince William.
"It would never happen with him in America," the insider said. "This gives them [an] opportunity to try and mend that bridge."
PRINCE WILLIAM ‘INCANDESCENT WITH ANGER’ AT PRINCE HARRY AS DIANA ANNIVERSARY DEEPENS ROYAL RIFT: PIERS MORGAN

Prince William, Prince of Wales, left, and Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, join the Procession following the State Hearse carrying the coffin of Queen Elizabeth II towards St George's Chapel on Sept. 19, 2022, in Windsor, England. But royal experts told Fox News Digital that Harry's reported plans to consider making a documentary about Princess Diana could threaten that opening, giving the Prince of Wales another reason to remain wary of his younger brother.

"I don't buy this," royal broadcaster Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "Harry says [he and his family] relocated for so many different reasons, but the main reason is clear: it's the reported planning of the Diana documentary for the 30th anniversary."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, sits in the stands during the Gallagher PREM 2026/2027 match between Leicester Tigers and Gloucester Rugby at Mattioli Woods Welford Road Stadium on Oct. 9, 2026, in Leicester, England. (Getty Images)

He doesn't want to speak so openly about Diana. And also, doing this would just drain him if he was going to do it as a working royal. He doesn't want to create publicity for Prince Harry's documentary, and he also doesn't want him and Harry pitted against each other as brothers."

Diana, Princess of Wales, died in 1997. She was 36. (Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and Kensington Palace for comment.
Several royal experts previously told Fox News Digital that the brothers have not been on speaking terms since 2022.
Prince William, left, is said to not be on speaking terms with his younger brother Prince Harry. (Mark Cuthbert/UK Press via Getty Images; Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

The Times recently reported that the Prince of Wales will not make a film about Princess Diana to mark the 30th anniversary of his mother's death in 2027, in part because he wants to avoid further conflict with Harry. According to the outlet, William has declined several offers to make or appear in documentaries about his mother.

Meanwhile, Harry is considering several projects to mark the 30th anniversary of Diana's death, People magazine reported. According to the outlet, the Duke of Sussex has been exploring how he can "most meaningfully" honor his mother and her legacy ahead of the Aug. 31, 2027, anniversary.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, meets members of the public as he arrives at The Community Recording Studio in Nottingham, England, during a visit with Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, on Oct. 15, 2026. (Getty Images)

Although several ideas are under discussion, People reported that no documentary has been finalized or confirmed. Harry has reached out to family members and friends connected to his late mother, several sources told the outlet.

I see the ruffling of Prince William's feathers. Prince William is entirely focused on his family and the long-term survival of the monarchy, but that's not to say that things can't change in the future."
Prince Harry's book "Spare" is displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

All three projects included personal revelations about life inside the royal family.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex leave after escorting the coffin of Queen Elizabeth II to Westminster Hall from Buckingham Palace for her lying in state, on Sept. 14, 2022, in London. "William deeply resents the way the Sussexes have monetized their royal connections," he said. "The Sussexes, as non-working royals, have the advantage as they are in situ and can do what they like. This does not mean that they will be accepted by the royal family in any of their activities in the coming months. … [But] it may be impossible to totally shut them out, given the international pull of their brand."

"Catherine may step into that breach and try to help, too, because she knows how important family is and how important Harry is to William," the source said. "She would want to see that healed, as any wife would. This gives them [an] opportunity to try and mend that bridge."

title: Kevin Bacon pleads for help recovering missing FedEx package rerouted multiple times around the globe

Kevin Bacon was yearning and burning for somebody to tell him where his lost clothes were hiding.
Bacon, 68, pleaded with his followers to help him figure out where FedEx sent a package of clothing he sent last month to a location across the pond.

"Hey everybody, it's me. I'm over here, I'm working in Ireland," Bacon told his followers. "I wanted to pack light, so I decided to ship some old clothes over here to Ireland. I don't buy a lot of clothes. I've had these clothes probably since the '90s.

"It went straight to Memphis, and then from Memphis it went to France, and by Sept. 28, it arrived in Germany, and by Sept. 29, they shipped it straight to Israel, not Ireland – Israel."

The "Footloose" actor went on to explain that the package traveled from Israel back to France on Oct. 3, only to be sent back to Israel the following day. It traveled to Germany on Oct. 5 before being routed back to Israel on Oct. 6.

title: Kristin Cavallari says she learned a painful $250K lesson involving her father at 22
summary: Kristin Cavallari revealed on her podcast how two six-figure loans to her father Dennis Cavallari were never repaid, leaving her $250,000 in the hole.
story: The Montana Boyz spoke to Fox News Digital at the CMT Music Awards about how Mark Estes relationship with Kristin Cavallari has helped the group.
Kristin Cavallari is reflecting on a painful lesson after lending her father a quarter of a million dollars.

During a recent episode of her podcast "Let's Be Honest with Kristin Cavallari," in which the 39-year-old reality star shared her opinions on women and finances, Cavallari recalled how she ended up $250,000 "in the hole" following two loans to her father Dennis Cavallari that were never repaid.
"My dad came to me — I was filming ‘The Hills,’ so I must have been 22 — and asked for a large sum of money to borrow. Six figures," she said.
Kristin Cavallari revealed that she loaned her father $250,000 and he never paid her back.  (GC Images)
KRISTIN CAVALLARI ADMITS HER KIDS FLY COACH WHILE SHE SITS IN FIRST CLASS
"And I was making great money at the time, but it’s still — I’m 22," Cavallari continued. "Six figures is a big deal for me."

"But I lent it to him, and he promised me he would pay me back," the Uncommon James founder remembered. "He probably said six months, and he was going to give me interest on top of it. And, you know, well, I didn’t get paid back. And instead, he asked to borrow more money, another six-figure number."
JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER CLAIMS HER EX-HUSBAND SECRETLY STOLE HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS FROM HER 'SOPRANOS' EARNINGS
Cavallari said that she confronted Dennis about not repaying the first loan but ultimately relented.

"I said to him, ‘You haven’t even acknowledged the first payment, and now you want more money?’" she recalled. "But because I’m such a f-----g sucker — or I was at the time — I lent him more money."
WYNONNA JUDD ADMITS HELPING DAUGHTER DURING METH BATTLE ‘BIT ME IN THE BUTT'
The "Laguna Beach" alum admitted she has no expectation of ever getting the money back.
"I will never see that money," she said. "So, when I tell you, I’m in the hole with my own dad, a quarter of a million dollars."
THE RICH HAVE ONE FINANCIAL HABIT MOST AMERICANS IGNORE AT THEIR PERIL
"Talk about a bad business decision," Cavallari added.
However, the TV personality acknowledged that the experience taught her the importance of setting boundaries with family and friends when it comes to money.
JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME

"I didn’t know how to set boundaries in my early 20s," she admitted. "I’ve learned that. You know, it would be a very different conversation probably today, but it’s the lending-money-to-people thing."
"The Hills" alum said she felt that her father "took advantage" of her.  (John Shearer/Getty Images for MTV.com)

"When you have money, it’s almost like people expect it," Cavallari continued. "And you are in no way, shape or form required or obligated to lend anybody money, especially if you’ve worked your f---king tail off for that money."
JENNIFER GARNER SAYS SHE 'PANICKED' ABOUT FINANCIAL STABILITY AFTER DIVORCE FROM BEN AFFLECK
"Like I have worked my ass off for all of my money," she added. "And so I think that’s why probably that stings the most."
"It just was like sort of taking advantage of me at such a young age."
CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT
Now a mother herself, Cavallari said she struggles to understand her father's decision to turn to her for such a large sum of money when she was so young.
Cavallari shares sons Camden, 14, and Jaxon, 12, and daughter Saylor, 10, with her ex-husband, former NFL quarterback Jay Cutler.
JENNIFER GARNER SAYS DIVORCE FROM BEN AFFLECK CAUSED 'UPHEAVAL' THAT KEPT HER FROM WORKING FOR YEARS
"I can’t imagine going to my kids when they’re 22 and asking for that kind of money," she said. "I guess I understand that he didn’t have a lot of options. But I don't know."

"And also my relationship with my dad is very complicated," Cavallari continued. "So there are other layers to it. But for the purpose of this conversation, I just think you’re allowed to do what you want to do with your money."
Cavallari said she learned an important lesson about setting boundaries with family regarding money.  (XNY/Star Max/GC Image)
Cavallari shared a clip from the episode on Instagram, emphasizing the importance of financial literacy for women.

"We’re talking all things MONEY this week!!" she wrote. "I’m over money being a taboo topic for women. We’re talking financial independence, the mistakes I’ve made, and everything I’ve learned along the way. If you wanna chase the bag, this one’s for you."
Cavallari previously discussed her difficult relationship with Dennis and the unpaid loans during a July appearance on the "Aspire with Emma Grede" podcast.
The "Balancing in Heels" author shared that she eventually came to terms with the financial loss.

"I've had to grapple with it, you know, and I've ultimately put it to bed and made peace with it," she said. "I think at the time, I didn't know how to say no to my dad. That's also been sort of like a big life lesson for me. I mean, I've ultimately cut my dad out of my life."

"So I really figured out how to say no to him," Cavallari continued. "But it was really hard for me when I was younger. And so, that's probably like the biggest thing that stands out in my mind in terms of how you think about teaching your kids about money."
Cavallari said she couldn't imagine asking her children for money when they are 22.  (Kristin Cavallari Instagram)

title: James McAvoy says he ‘nearly died’ after his lungs collapsed following botched biopsy
summary: James McAvoy revealed how a "botched" lung biopsy nearly killed him and led to weeks in the hospital before he underwent an intense physical transformation for his "Glass" role.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
James McAvoy opened up about a life-threatening health scare that left him hospitalized for several weeks after what he described as a botched medical procedure.

During a recent appearance on Dax Shepard's "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 47-year-old actor recalled how he pushed his body to its limits for his transformation into the Beast in 2019's "Glass" after first recovering from a serious infection and collapsed lungs.
"I'd actually been in hospital and I had a lung puncture because… they saw a shadow in my lung, so they wanted to biopsy it to see if it was cancer, which it wasn't, which was great," McAvoy said.
"But that was botched, and I nearly died," he continued. "I was at home two days later and my lungs just collapsed in bed one night, and I was on my own as well, so it was crazy."
SHARON STONE CLAIMS EX-HUSBAND SIGNED HER UP FOR BRAIN SURGERY WITHOUT HER CONSENT AFTER STROKE
James McAvoy said a botched lung biopsy nearly killed him.  (Getty Images for IMDb)
The "X-Men: First Class" star said he spent two or three weeks in the hospital while doctors worked unsuccessfully to clear his lungs.

"They tried everything to clean out," McAvoy recalled. "Nothing was working. So, they were like, 'We're going to need to cut you open big-style. Go in with like soapy, like dish soap basically, and just like clean you out, scoop it all out.'"
McAvoy said his lungs collapsed while he was alone in bed. (Dave Benett/WireImage)

McAvoy recalled that after his medical ordeal, he underwent an intense process for the next four or five months as he bulked up to reprise his role in "Glass." In the M. Night Shyamalan-directed movie, the actor portrayed Kevin Wendell Crumb, who suffers from severe dissociative identity disorder (DID) with 24 distinct personalities.
MATT DAMON REFUSES TO PUT BODY IN 'DANGEROUS' SITUATIONS FOR HOLLYWOOD ROLES AFTER TURNING 50

McAvoy first played Wendell in 2016's "Split," which was the sequel to 2000's "Unbreakable." In "Split," Wendell's 24th personality "The Beast," who possesses superhuman strength, speed, durability and pain suppression, became the central threat after emerging toward the end of the film.
"Unlike ‘Split,’ I was the Beast, like most of the movie," McAvoy recalled. "So I was like, 'I'm really going to need to do the real thing. I'm going to need to go for it.'"
'THE ODYSSEY' STAR MATT DAMON REVEALS BRUTAL SIX-MONTH TRANSFORMATION BEHIND CHRISTOPHER NOLAN FILM
"I remember saying to [Shyamalan] like, ‘You’re going to need to get me a trainer,'" he said.
The "Split" star said he spent weeks in the hospital before undergoing an intense physical transformation for his role in "Glass."  (Getty Images)
McAvoy explained that Shyamalan offered to hire a trainer from "the local gym," but he rejected that idea.
'SUITS' STAR RICK HOFFMAN REVEALS 'INTENSE' ROUTINE BEHIND DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION
McAvoy said he had worked with trainers from local gyms before but needed someone who could transform his physique into that of a figure from Greek mythology.
"The guy that worked with me was amazing," he added. "He didn't move in with me, but he was just with me a lot and kind of regulated what I ate and trained me just right."

"For the first four weeks, he rehabilitated me. I could walk, but I couldn’t run, couldn’t cycle, couldn’t jog," McAvoy recalled. "So he did a lot of rehabilitation and, sort of, functional movement, and then put the pounds on me really fast."
McAvoy said he couldn't run or jog at the beginning of his training. (Getty Images for IMDb)
McAvoy recently claimed that he was bullied on the set of the hit HBO miniseries "Band of Brothers."

While recently appearing on "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen," McAvoy was asked to rate his experience working on different projects, and when he was shown a picture of the show's cast, he recalled that one of his co-stars organized a group to mock him on set.

"On my first day on set, there was a ton of actors," he began. "It was one of those scenes with everybody in it, and we’re all at a bar, and I had a scene. And all these guys were in it for nine months, 10 months, and they get one line in one episode, and one line 10 episodes later. They were all pissed. I come in for one episode, and I’ve got an arc and scenes. I’ve got tons of lines."

When the photo, which featured many of his co-stars from the show, flashed on the screen, McAvoy confirmed that a specific actor was in the photo.

While he didn't name names, the photo featured Donnie Wahlberg, Kirk Acevedo, Scott Grimes, Neal McDonough, Adam James, Frank John Hughes, Philip Barantini and Ross McCall.

title: Cindy Crawford mourns son Presley Gerber in heartbreaking tribute
summary: Cindy Crawford called Presley Gerber a "sweet, beautiful soul" in an emotional Instagram tribute weeks after his death at a rehabilitation facility.
story: Presley Gerber, model and son of Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27 in a Los Angeles rehab facility. TMZ executive producer Michael Babcock joins 'America's Newsroom' to discuss the ongoing investigation into Gerber's death as a suspected overdose. The tragedy follows Gerber's previous public statements regarding his mental health and substance abuse struggles.
Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and Kaia Gerber are remembering their late son and brother, Presley Walker Gerber, as a "sweet, beautiful soul" in heartbreaking tributes shared weeks after his death.
"Presley Walker Gerber. July 2, 1999—September 20, 2026," Crawford wrote on Instagram, alongside a photo of her son.

"We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother. We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years," she continued. "He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever."
Crawford praised Presley for "how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability" and thanked the public for supporting the family since the devastating loss.
GEORGE CLOONEY SAYS FAMILY IS STILL PROCESSING PRESLEY GERBER'S TRAGIC DEATH
Presley Gerber died Sept. 20. He was 27.  (WWD via Getty Images)

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," the model wrote. "Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia."
PRESLEY GERBER DEAD AT 27: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT CINDY CRAWFORD, RANDE GERBER'S FAMILY
Kaia, Presley’s younger sister, shared her own tribute on Instagram, describing her brother as her "ultimate teacher," "best buddy" and "great protector."
Presley Gerber was the only son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber. (Alberto Rodriguez/Variety via Getty Images)
CHAD LOWE’S DAUGHTER MABEL SHARES HEARTBREAKING TRIBUTE TO LATE SISTER FIONA, 13
"I don’t have the words," Kaia wrote. "And maybe the tiny mercy is that we didn’t need them all along. Words fail and words subtract and words summarize and words always lack truth."

"You know how much i loved being your sister: it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself. i came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. i had more love for you than i knew what to do with. and now that it has nowhere obvious to go, i’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole."
"you believed — always believed — in people. you met cruelty not with anger, but with confusion. and curiosity. you believed people were inherently good because, presley, you are inherently good."
Kaia recalled being scared to get her ears pierced when the two were younger.
"i got scared before getting my ears pierced, so you went first. you always went first. but when i held the earring they took from your body, all i could think was: that belongs to you."
Rande Gerber, Kaia Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Presley Gerber attend The Fashion Awards 2018 in partnership with Swarovski at Royal Albert Hall on Dec. 10, 2018, in London, England. (Getty Images)
"and i really f—ing wish you hadn’t gone first this time."
In another passage, Kaia said she was still learning how to be Presley’s sister "in a world that I can’t reach for you in."
"I don’t know how to do that yet," she wrote.
She ended the tribute with a series of heartbreaking declarations.
"My darling brother. I do adore you," Kaia wrote. "I love my brother. My brother is dead."
"And this party sucks so bad without you, prez," she added.
Gerber died Sept. 20 at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford's son, died Sept. 20, 2026. He was 27. (Paul Archuleta)
PRESLEY GERBER’S FINAL HOURS AT REHAB IN FOCUS AMID CAUSE OF DEATH QUESTIONS
The model's cause of death was "deferred," according to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.
The medical examiner told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available."
PRESLEY GERBER’S DEATH SPARKS QUESTIONS ABOUT OVERDOSE, WITHDRAWAL AND REHAB SAFETY
Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department.
A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."
GEORGE CLOONEY RUSHES TO RANDE GERBER AND CINDY CRAWFORD'S SIDE AFTER SON PRESLEY'S DEATH
Months before his death, Presley Gerber shared a raw look at his battle with addiction and the treatment he hoped would help him find his way back to himself.
In March, the model posted a video of himself preparing to undergo an "ibogaine flood dose," a psychedelic treatment, at a wellness clinic in Cancún, Mexico.

According to Stanford Medicine, ibogaine is a naturally occurring psychedelic derived from the root bark of the Tabernanthe iboga shrub. It has "gained interest from the medical and scientific communities for its potential to treat opioid and cocaine addiction, and research has suggested that it increases signaling of several important molecules within the brain, some of which have been linked to drug addiction and depression."

Kaia Gerber, Rande Gerber, model Cindy Crawford and Presley Gerber attend Rock4EB! 2015 with Ed Sheeran and David Spade on Nov. 15, 2015, in Malibu, California. (Todd Williamson/Getty Images for EB Kids)
The treatment is legal in some countries, but not in the United States.
"Quiet moment before everything changed," Presley Gerber wrote in the Instagram caption. "I was absolutely terrified, and I knew I would be again if I ever had to face something like this."
Gerber said letting go of control was difficult, but he trusted "there was something bigger than me guiding it."
CARA DELEVINGNE ADMITS SHE USED PARTY DRUG GHB DAILY BEFORE TERRIFYING SEIZURES FORCED HER SOBER
"I knew why I was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself," he wrote.
He also said he was "praying it’s the last time" he would need to return for treatment.

Presley Gerber’s post was one of several instances in which he publicly documented his recovery journey. In recent years, he had spoken candidly about depression, panic attacks, addiction and the challenges of seeking treatment.
During a 2023 episode of the "Studio 22" podcast, Presley Gerber discussed his experiences with depression and other mental health challenges.
Rande Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Presley Walker Gerber attend Chanel Dinner Celebrating our Majestic Oceans, A Benefit for NRDC on June 2, 2018, in Malibu, California.  (Stefanie Keenan/WireImage)
"[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It’s a 24/7 job, and there’s so much to it," he said.

"That’s really what I want to do is help people, whether you’re depressed, you’re struggling with something that is having a negative effect on your body," he continued. "I mean it could be anything, and there’s no judgment."
Gerber said he hoped his experiences could help other people avoid making similar mistakes.

"I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things," he said. "What I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people, so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made."
He also explained why he wanted to be open about his mental health journey.

title: Jana Kramer says Los Angeles priced her out of the childhood she wanted for her kids
summary: Jana Kramer reveals why she left Studio City for Nashville, giving her kids the Midwest-style childhood she cherished while growing up in Michigan.
story: The actress admitted to Fox News Digital she couldn't afford to give her kids the childhood she wanted for them when living in Los Angeles.
Jana Kramer is opening up about not being able to afford to give her children the life she wanted for them.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 42-year-old actress spoke about her new film, "The One," and how moving to Nashville, Tennessee has allowed her to give her kids the childhood she had.

"I remember being in Studio City with the two kids, and we couldn't afford to have a bigger place with a bigger backyard and neighborhoods like that. Again, we just couldn't afford certain neighborhoods and, for me, Tennessee has just always been a place that every time I land, my nervous system just like relaxes, it feels calm," she said.

As someone who grew up in the Midwest, she "struggled" with the idea that some of her "greatest memories as a child" included running around her "neighborhood and just going from friend's house to friend's house," and staying out playing "until the sun went down."
Kramer recalled not being able to afford the life she wanted to give her children when living in Los Angeles. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
JANA KRAMER SAYS HOLDING ON TO TOXIC RELATIONSHIPS 'DRAINS YOU' UNTIL YOU ‘START LOSING YOURSELF' COMPLETELY

After moving to Tennessee, she said it now brings her joy to watch her children having a similar childhood, spending their days "on their bikes and going to their friends houses," noting "it just makes me feel like home."
"I love it here. You can always go back," she added. "You can always go to Hollywood, but things have changed so much with self-tapes, which I actually don't love, but you can. It's a plane away."
WATCH: Jana Kramer moved to Nashville to give her kids a taste of her Midwestern childhood
The "One Tree Hill" star explained that while she knows many people who are raising their children in Los Angeles, and "that's amazing for them," she enjoys the "totally different life" in Tennessee.
She attributes her affinity towards Tennessee to her own upbringing in Michigan, noting she values how she was raised, "that I just really wanted that same upbringing for my kids."

title: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded messages for his kids as cancer threatened to take his tongue
summary: Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded goodbye messages for his young children after doctors discussed removing his tongue to fight throat cancer.
story: Facing the possibility of losing his tongue, Poison drummer Rikki Rockett recorded messages for his kids. Now, he's celebrating 10 years cancer-free. Rockett is the author of a new memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison."
Poison drummer Rikki Rockett was staring down a terrifying possibility as he battled cancer: Doctors might have to remove his tongue.
After chemotherapy and radiation failed to stop the disease, the rocker began recording messages for his young children so they could remember the sound of his voice.

"I was recording pieces of information for my kids so they could watch it, because the next step was to cut my tongue out if they had to," Rockett (born Richard Allan Ream) told Fox News Digital. "And I wanted them to know what I sounded like and my advice to them growing up, and I wanted them to hear it from me. I wanted them to understand what I was, what I thought I was or would become."
HOW THE NELSON TWINS WENT FROM PACKING ARENAS TO BEING 'F---ING BROKE' DESPITE MAKING MILLIONS
Poison, from left: Bobby Dall, C.C. DeVille, Bret Michaels and Rikki Rockett, circa 1987. Rockett has written a memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison." (Courtesy Everett Collection)
Rockett, whose weight dropped to 161 pounds during treatment, said the possibility of losing his tongue left him fearing he might not survive much longer.

"I would've most likely had a feeding tube," he said. "I don't think I would've lived much longer. It would've added another year or two. Some people do make it. Some people get all of that done and live for a long time. But I think a lot of times, with the way it was going with me, I don't think I would've survived, quite honestly."
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
Rikki Rockett's memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison," is available now. (Rare Bird Books)
Now 65, Rockett says he has been free of cancer for a decade. His memoir, "Ghost Notes: My Life in Poison," chronicles his rise to stardom during the decadent '80s and his grueling health battle.
WATCH: POISON DRUMMER RIKKI ROCKETT RECALLS HEARTBREAKING CANCER BATTLE
In 2015, Rockett said he and his family developed sore throats. They were all prescribed antibiotics, but while everyone else recovered, his symptoms persisted.
Rockett returned to the doctor, who examined his nose and throat with a scope. During the examination, the doctor spotted something suspicious.
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs at Oracle Arena in Oakland, California, on June 13, 2017. (Alamy Stock Photo)
"I don't know if it's cancer, but it's suspicious, and we got to do a biopsy," Rockett recalled his doctor telling him. "My life changed at that very second."
Before his cancer diagnosis, Rikki Rockett had a persistent sore throat that lasted for months. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)
According to the Head and Neck Cancer Alliance, Rockett was diagnosed with HPV-related throat cancer in 2015. The disease affected the base of his tongue.

According to his memoir, Rockett had experienced a sore throat and a swollen lymph node for more than a month. It hurt every time he swallowed. After doctors diagnosed him with cancer, he received radiation and chemotherapy.
Rikki Rockett attends the First Annual Concrete Foundations Awards on Oct. 3, 1991, at the Los Angeles Airport Marriott Hotel. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"Before long, I couldn't eat solid food anymore," he wrote. "My weight dropped dramatically because all I could manage was soup, shakes and water. Eventually, I couldn't eat or drink anything at all."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Rikki Rockett feared losing his tongue and time with his beloved children. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

Rockett wrote: "I've got throat cancer. At its worst, I struggle to swallow even a gulp of water. This morning, my son had to watch tears running down my cheeks as I tried to eat a spoonful of soup. He looked terrified."

Rockett told Fox News Digital that he eventually "wound up in stage 4." For three months, he received radiation five days a week, along with chemotherapy weekly, but he said the treatment failed. Doctors then discussed removing his tongue, according to Rockett.
Poison drummer Rikki Rockett performs at The Wharf in Orange Beach, on July 7, 2011. (Alamy Live News)
Rockett was terrified. In his memoir, he wrote that he believed he had only a "40 or 50 percent chance of living." But he refused to give up.
From left: C.C. DeVille, Bret Michaels, Rikki Rockett, and Bobby Dall of Poison are seen here at SiriusXM Studios on Dec. 4, 2019, in Los Angeles. (Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"Even with all the treatment, it still didn't work," he recalled. "So then I got on an experimental drug combination at UC San Diego Moores Cancer Center, and it worked incredibly well. It's one of those things where, if it works, it's amazing. If it doesn't, you kind of go, 'Wow, maybe I wasted my time.' So I had to roll the dice. And I did. And when I rolled it, thankfully, it came out in my favor."

According to UC San Diego Health, Rockett participated in a clinical trial involving a combination of two drugs: pembrolizumab (Keytruda) and epacadostat. Rockett was declared free of throat cancer in July 2016.
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs onstage during The Stadium Tour at Truist Park in Atlanta, on June 16, 2022. (Getty Images for Live Nation)
The treatment took a toll. At one point, Rockett's tongue swelled so much that he feared he might choke. Soon, however, a scan offered hope.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Rikki Rockett is seen here during his cancer fight. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

"The crazy thing was that my first PET scan showed that 90 percent of the cancer was already gone," Rockett wrote. "And by the second PET scan, it was all gone. It was as if the angels had come down and blessed me. I mean, it was unbelievable."
Members of Poison — Bret Michaels, C.C. DeVille, Rikki Rockett and Bobby Dall — pose on the red carpet at the 1987 MTV Music Video Awards in Universal City, California. (Getty Images)
Rockett wrote that his doctor seemed just as surprised by the results but explained that treatment needed to continue to reduce the risk of the cancer returning.
But Rockett's health challenges were far from over.
Rikki Rocket attends the Frankie Banali of Quiet Riot bronze statue unveiling and memorial at Rainbow Bar & Grill on Nov. 14, 2021, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images)
"Some eight months into the process, nothing was coming up, but I was getting high white blood cell counts," Rockett wrote.

"So, they got concerned about that, and to cut a long story short, I wound up with something called CML, chronic myeloid leukemia, and it’s a predisposition thing. It’s a translocation between BCR-ABL, the chromosomes. You’re prone to it if, like me, you have the Philadelphia chromosome. Of course, it absolutely freaked me out. I mean, I just went through one cancer, and now I was facing another one."
Rikki Rockett told Fox News Digital he's been cancer-free for 10 years. (WireImage)
Chronic myeloid leukemia is a type of blood cancer often associated with an acquired genetic abnormality known as the Philadelphia chromosome.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
American glam rock band Poison, including Bret Michaels, Rikki Rockett, C.C. DeVille and Bobby Dall, performs at Joe Louis Arena in Detroit, on Jan. 9, 1987. (Getty Images)

"The hematologist, however, took everything in stride, and when we met, she was super calm," he wrote. "She told me, ‘You picked the best leukemia you could. It’s very treatable, and sometimes curable.’ Dr. Jaimeson would be my doctor for the very long foreseeable future, and I was blessed to have her."
Rikki Rockett of Poison performs at Five Points Amphitheatre in Irvine, California, on May 18, 2018. (Getty Images)

"So, all that happened was that she put me on new medication, which I’m still on. It has some nasty side effects, but the best side effect is that CML has been 100 percent in remission! Zero detection for a number of years now! There must be a reason why I’m still here, I think to this day."
Looking back, Rockett told Fox News Digital his medical team "actually saved my life."
Rikki Rockett of Poison is seen here at the Anaheim Convention Center in Anaheim, California, on Jan. 22, 2026. (Getty Images)

Rockett still lives with the lasting effects of his treatment. But a decade after his throat cancer battle, he's focused less on what the disease took from him and more on what he lived to see — his children growing up.
"Sometimes my voice gets rough, or I get dry," he said. "I get very dry because my salivary glands got toasted with the radiation. But I’m cancer-free, and I’ve been cancer free for 10 years."
Drummer Rikki Rockett attends the 2013 NAMM Show at the Anaheim Convention Center on Jan. 24, 2013. (Getty Images for NAMM)
Rockett has no plans to slow down. He's been keeping busy performing with his band, Rockett Mafia.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Rikki Rockett hopes his memoir will encourage readers not to give up. (Courtesy of Rikki Rockett)

"I’m not out of gas yet," he said with a smile. "I still got stuff to do. And I love playing because I want my kids to see me, and they have. They’ve been to some Poison concerts. I wanted them to see me, and they did. I got that wish."
For Rockett, beating cancer meant getting the time he once feared he wouldn’t have. And he's not wasting a single second, he insisted.
Rikki Rockett is seen here with his daughter. (Instagram.com/rikkirockett)
"A big part of it was fighting for my kids," he reflected. "There’s no question that was a big chunk of my fight."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: William Shatner finds answer to 'What the f--- is heavy metal?' after forming new band at 95
summary: William Shatner, 95, reveals his upcoming heavy metal album "What the F is Heavy Metal" features Queen's Brian May and over 50 musicians joining the project.
story: "Star Trek" icon William Shatner explains how Cleopatra Records inspired his heavy-metal project, which features more than 50 musicians, including Brian May, and led to the formation of his band, The *uckers.
William Shatner is showing no signs of slowing down as he prepares to front a heavy metal band at age 95.

In addition to his decades-long career as an actor, Shatner is also an accomplished musician, who has released 11 studio albums encompassing a wide range of genres including spoken word, rock, progressive rock, Christmas and country releases.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, Shatner, who recently partnered with over-the-counter hearing aid maker Audien Hearing for a new campaign, shared his reaction when his music label Cleopatra Records first approached him earlier this year about making a heavy metal album.
WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE'
"I said, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal?’" the "Star Trek" icon recalled.
William Shatner explained why he decided to launch a heavy metal band at age 95.  (WireImage)
"And that's the title of the album, ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner added.
COUNTRY MUSIC SINGER SHANE SMITH PUTS HIS OWN SPIN ON JOHNNY CASH'S ICONIC 'HURT' COVER

Shatner told Fox News Digital that he teamed up with his longtime creative collaborator and friend, author Robert Sharenow, for the project. The two previously worked together on five albums featuring autobiographical lyrics and spoken-word performances.
"So we wrote six songs for the album," Shatner said. "And I laid down my track."
WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER, 95, ANSWERS ‘WHAT THE F--- IS HEAVY METAL?' WITH NEW ALBUM
In addition to six original songs, Shatner said that "What the F is Heavy Metal" will feature covers with contributions from more than 50 musicians,

"We've got one number in the album that's gonna be out in the wintertime called ‘What the F is Heavy Metal,’" Shatner said. "All of a sudden, 50, I'm told 50 heavy metal musicians all volunteer to be on this album."
PAUL MCCARTNEY REVEALS HOW A 'HAPPY' TEEN HITCHHIKING TRIP WITH GEORGE HARRISON DELIVERED A SHOCK

The musicians included Queen's Brian May, who performed a guitar solo for one of the album's tracks titled "Rage." Shatner explained that "Rage" features the famous line "Rage, rage against the dying of the light" from the 1951 poem "Do not go gentle into that good night," written by Welsh poet Dylan Thomas.
Marcus Nand and Britt Lightning of The *uckers perform with William Shatner during Riot Fest at Douglass Park in Chicago, Ill., on Sept. 20, 2026. (WireImage)

While speaking with Fox News Digital, Shatner recalled that he was later invited to perform at Riot Fest, an annual three-day punk rock music festival held at Douglass Park in Chicago, Illinois. In a July social media post, the organizers of Riot Fest announced that Shatner would debut his heavy metal band The *uckers at the festival, noting that they had tried to book him for over a decade.
ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES

The "Boston Legal" alum said that his label tapped five musicians to form his new heavy metal band. The all-star rock and heavy metal lineup includes guitarists Marcus Nand and Britt Lightning, bassist Phil Soussan and drummer Fred Aching.
"They put together a group of fabulous musicians," Shatner said. "We call ourselves The *uckers for, you know, ‘What the f--- is heavy metal.’'"
BRET MICHAELS CANCELS REMAINING 2026 TOUR DATES HOURS AFTER 'COMEBACK' PERFORMANCE DUE TO HEALTH SCARE
Shatner's upcoming album will feature 50 heavy metal musicians.  (WireImage)

The band made its live debut in Chicago on Sept. 19 and performed at Riot Fest the following day. The *uckers played original songs including "Rage," "Sky" and "One Fear" alongside covers of Ozzy Osbourne's "Crazy Train," Motörhead's "Ace of Spades," and Metallica's "Enter Sandman."
"We went to Riot Fest … and was a huge success, huge," Shatner recalled. "They were cheering and the reviews and the people…so it proved to me the viability of ‘What the F is Heavy Metal.'"
‘A MAN WITHOUT LOVE’ SINGER ENGELBERT HUMPERDINCK CREDITS UNDERWATER WORKOUT FOR KEEPING HIM ‘ALIVE’ AT 90
After performing with The *uckers and making his heavy metal album, Shatner said he has an answer to his original question.
"It is the beat of life," he said. "It is such an energetic way of doing music. It enlivens your life. It stirs you up. It makes you pay attention."
WATCH: WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HEAVY METAL ‘ENLIVENS’ HIS LIFE AS HE FRONTS BAND AT 95

Shatner explained that his approach to heavy metal extends beyond the music itself. For the album, he said he incorporated fresh takes on the lyrics of several classic songs, including Metallica’s "Enter Sandman," which he believes contains darker themes beneath its familiar melody.
"I've reinterpreted even the cover songs," he said.
Shatner said his version of "Enter Sandman" focuses on the sinister implications of the song’s lyrics rather than treating the Sandman as a harmless bedtime figure.
"It's a total reinterpretation of the Sandman," he said. "It is amazing."
Shatner and The *uckers performed for the first time in Chicago in September. (WireImage)

While Shatner is embracing the volume of heavy metal, the project also connects to a more personal issue. The actor is partnering with Audien Hearing on a campaign about hearing health after experiencing tinnitus and hearing loss himself.

Shatner recalled that his hearing challenges began decades ago on the set of "Star Trek." During the filming of an explosion scene featuring him alongside his co-star Leonard Nimoy, the stage doors were accidentally left closed, preventing the blast from dissipating properly.

He told Fox News Digital that the two actors were taken to a doctor after their ears began ringing. Shatner said that he did not immediately realize that the noise had become permanent. The Canada native recalled that while walking on the beach one day, he noticed that the hiss of the retreating waves never completely disappeared.
"I heard the hiss, but the hiss never went away," he said. "It was always hissing."
The actor said the album features reinterpreted versions of hit heavy metal songs.  (Getty Images)

Shatner said he eventually learned to live with the tinnitus through a process known as habituation. He also estimated that he has lost roughly 20% to 30% of his hearing and said hearing aids have helped him rediscover everyday sounds.
"The dog claws on the floor, the creak of this rocking chair — all the panoply of sounds that go to make up the richness of the world around us, we’re using hearing," he said.
Shatner's hearing challenges have not stopped him from playing heavy metal. However, he said the loud music can temporarily intensify the tinnitus, which he noticed after performing at Riot Fest.
"Now I'm fitted with earphones, right? And the sound would have been blasting in anyway, but it's heavy metal sound," he said. "I'm blasting in on my tinnitus."

title: ‘Super-drug’ 10 times stronger than fentanyl linked to deaths across multiple states
summary: Cychlorphine, a synthetic opioid reportedly up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl, has been linked to at least 55 deaths across the U.S.
story: Nicholas Kardaras, Ph.D., shared the life-threatening risks of called cychlorphine, which he calls "the new fentanyl on steroids."
A powerful new synthetic opioid said to be more potent than fentanyl has been linked to dozens of recent deaths in the U.S., prompting warnings from health officials.
Tennessee was an early hotspot, with the state’s health department announcing in March that more than 30 fatal overdoses had been associated with cychlorphine since October 2025.
An April 2026 notice from the White House’s Office of National Drug Control Policy cited at least 41 Tennessee deaths between July 2025 and February 2026 and at least 55 deaths nationally.
KRATOM INDUSTRY WARNS SYNTHETIC OPIOIDS SHOULD NOT BE CALLED 'KRATOM'
Fatal overdoses have also been reported in Illinois, California and Oklahoma, according to public health and law enforcement records.
A powerful new synthetic opioid said to be more potent than fentanyl has been linked to dozens of recent deaths in the U.S. (iStock)
"Cychlorphine is particularly dangerous due to its strength, where a very small amount can cause someone to stop breathing," the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health said in its advisory.

Nicholas Kardaras, Ph.D., CEO and chief clinical officer of the New York Center for Living in Manhattan and a clinical professor at Stony Brook Medicine’s School of Social Welfare, called cychlorphine "the new fentanyl on steroids."
WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT PENTOBARBITAL AFTER DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES

Cychlorphine is a novel, unregulated synthetic opioid that activates the same receptors as fentanyl, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration. It can cause profound sedation, slowed or stopped breathing, or death.
The drug is not approved for medical use and has been detected in illicit drugs and counterfeit pills.
Younger people may face greater exposure because some are more likely to experiment with drugs or purchase counterfeit pills. (iStock)
Kardaras called cychlorphine "one of the most potent synthetic opioids" now appearing in the illicit drug supply.

"Fentanyl is about 50 times more potent than morphine or heroin," he told Fox News Digital. "Cychlorphine is reportedly up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl — so theoretically, about 500 times more potent than morphine or heroin."
"This new synthetic drug is making fentanyl look like yesterday's candy."
DR DREW PINSKY REVEALS RED FLAG IN PRESLEY GERBER ADDICTION TREATMENT BEFORE MODEL'S DEATH
Cychlorphine is taken in various forms — people can ingest it as a pill, snort it in powder form or crush it and administer it intravenously, according to Kardaras.
"The problem has been, in addition to its potency, it's often put in other designer drugs and in counterfeit pills," he cautioned.
"It's a constant battle of keeping up with the latest iterations of new drugs."
While some people seek out cychlorphine for its potency, others may ingest it unknowingly when it is mixed into other substances.
"Sometimes, by talking about how potent some of these substances are, we increase the allure of them for some addicts, unfortunately," Kardaras said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
While cychlorphine is primarily a street drug, it can also be purchased online or via "boutique designer-drug markets," according to the expert.

Cychlorphine can cause a fatal overdose in anyone, regardless of age. Kardaras said younger people may face greater exposure because some are more likely to experiment with drugs or purchase counterfeit pills.
While some people seek out cychlorphine for its potency, others may ingest it unknowingly when it is mixed into other substances. (iStock)
"They’re buying something online … and all of a sudden, without knowing it, they’re ingesting fentanyl or another synthetic opioid," he said.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Naloxone, commonly sold under the brand name Narcan, can reverse cychlorphine’s opioid effects, but multiple or prolonged doses may be needed.
"What used to take one or two doses of Narcan to reverse an overdose may now require five or six doses, based on anecdotal evidence," Kardaras said.
Another major concern with cychlorphine is that standard fentanyl test strips and routine hospital opioid urine screens do not detect it. (iStock)
The DEA advises people to administer naloxone immediately, call 911 and be prepared to give additional doses.
Another major concern with cychlorphine is that standard fentanyl test strips and routine hospital opioid urine screens do not detect it.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Most drug tests have very specific chemical structures that they detect in any kind of synthetic or non-synthetic drug, and this new one hasn't quite been baked into the current testing strips," Kardaras noted.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The takeaway, he said, is that cychlorphine may be up to 10 times more potent than fentanyl, is not detected by standard fentanyl test strips or routine hospital opioid urine screens, and may require multiple doses of naloxone to reverse.
"So it's a triple whammy," he said. "It's a constant battle of keeping up with the latest iterations of new drugs."
